label: C. Buyer Path with RFQ Rail
prompt:
Create a high-fidelity desktop homepage visual composition for an English-language B2B industrial fan supplier website. This is a complete web UI screenshot at 1536 × 1024, not a poster and not a standalone product photo.

Use the referenced image only to preserve the established visual world: warm white and near-white background, deep navy typography, muted teal technical accents, safety-orange calls to action, realistic industrial fan imagery, precise thin rules, matte industrial materials, strong condensed display typography paired with a clean humanist sans serif. Do not copy the referenced page composition or content layout.

Composition concept: ‘Buyer Path with RFQ Rail.’ Use a compact top navigation with a text-only wordmark ‘XINGXU FAN’, navigation links Products, Applications, For Distributors, Resources, About, and an orange Request a Quote button.

Directly below the navigation, create a compact full-width trust introduction rather than a conventional split hero. On the left use ‘Quanzhou Xingxu Fan & Ventilation Supply’ and the headline ‘Nearly 30 Years of Hands-On Fan Supply’. On the right use this exact supporting copy: ‘Industrial fan supply, selection advice and sourcing support for distributors, contractors and equipment manufacturers in Malaysia and the Philippines.’ Add a restrained ‘REAL BUSINESS EVIDENCE’ micro-strip with four clearly marked placeholder chips: ‘Storefront Photo’, ‘Warehouse Photo’, ‘Product Photo’, ‘Nameplate Photo’; each must visibly say ‘PLACEHOLDER’.

Below that introduction, use an original two-part working interface:
- The wide left area is a product-selection canvas headed ‘Choose a Fan Category’. Across its top, include buyer-path tabs ‘Distributors’, ‘Engineering Contractors’, and ‘Equipment Manufacturers’, with ‘Distributors’ visually active. Show three large editorial product panels using realistic industrial fan images and only these category names: ‘Negative Pressure Fans’, ‘Axial Fans’, and ‘Centrifugal Fans’. Use no model numbers or specifications.
- The narrower right side is a persistent pale-navy technical quotation rail titled ‘Start an RFQ’. It must look like a real web form and contain clearly labelled empty controls for ‘Product Category’, ‘Quantity’, ‘Specifications / Parameters’, and ‘Destination’. Include a dominant orange button ‘Submit Inquiry’. Beneath it, show a small contact-choice row with text labels only: ‘WhatsApp’, ‘Facebook’, ‘Gmail’, ‘WeChat’; no handles or account details.

At the lower edge, show a precise three-item service bar containing only ‘Selection Advice’, ‘Cross-Brand Sourcing’, and ‘Export Packaging & Logistics Coordination’. Keep trust first, product clarity second, and inquiry efficiency third.

Use only these factual claims: the business has operated for approximately 30 years; it supplies industrial fans; it offers selection advice, cross-brand sourcing, export packaging coordination and logistics coordination; target customers are distributors, contractors and equipment manufacturers in Malaysia and the Philippines. Do not invent a founding year, model numbers, technical specifications, prices, certifications, client logos, customer counts, export history, factory claims, manufacturing claims, awards, flags, maps, or contact handles. Remove decorative fan-shaped logo marks and avoid generic abstract gradients, glassmorphism, excessive rounded cards, a template-like SaaS hero, and vague marketing slogans. Make all English UI text legible, align fields precisely, and make the page feel distinctive, credible, practical and premium.
